subject: BrightBay vendor transition — trade-in credit structure & SLA uplift
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@brightbay.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBay Procurement <procurement@brightbay.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: vendor swap economics and trade-in credit

Diego —

Thanks for the intro last week. BrightBay is finalizing a preferred vendor decision and we want to understand a pragmatic commercial structure if we move from our incumbent (CloudForge) to Redwood. Two quick asks up front:

1) Can you outline a trade-in credit approach for existing committed spend on CloudForge? We need a simple, auditable construct for procurement.
2) We care about SLA uplift (p99 latency and availability) — what guardrails/credits do you attach for mission-critical endpoints?

We have a commercial review with our CPO on Thursday. Can you get something over by Wednesday EOD PT? I attached our internal TCO snapshot.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Strategy
BrightBay

Attachment: BrightBay_TCO_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@brightbay.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, BrightBay Procurement <procurement@brightbay.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: vendor swap economics and trade-in credit

Ellen —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the TCO. Quick summary of what I can put on paper by Wednesday: a tiered trade-in credit tied to remaining committed term, plus an SLA uplift menu that maps to service credits. High level: 

- Trade-in credit: up to 30% of remaining committed spend, graded by remaining term (shorter remaining term = smaller credit). We’ll provide an amortized worksheet to show reconciliation mechanics.
- SLA uplift: baseline (99.9% availability, standard p99) included; optional 99.95% with higher priority routing and 3% monthly credit on missed SLOs; 99.99% available for enterprise pilots with 7% credit on missed SLOs.

I’m looping in Priyom to confirm floor economics and Laura/Hannah for contract/SOW items. If the procurement team can share the incumbent contract excerpt (just the committed spend lines), that will speed the credit math.

I’ll attach a draft term-sheet and a short SOW for the pilot.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: transition-credit-term-sheet.xlsx (term sheet stub), Redwood-Draft-SOW-v1.pdf (SOW stub)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightBay — proposed commercial levers

Diego —

Solid first pass. A couple of internal notes on the credit math: 

1) Margin floor: we should not go below a 38% gross margin after credits for a 12-month ramp pilot. If BrightBay expects deeper credits, we need a minimum commit or usage-based true-up at 12 months.
2) Term weighting: propose we cap trade-in credits for contracts older than 18 months to 20% (to avoid indemnifying heavy discounts on legacy deals).
3) SLA credits: reduce the high-tier miss-credit from 7% to 5% — we can still offer the routing priority without taking on outsized refund risk.

If we take those constraints, we can sign-off on the term-sheet. I’ll let Laura flag any legal caveats.

— Priyom
Director, Commercial Operations

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 07:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BrightBay — proposed commercial levers (need quick review)

Hannah / Laura —

Forwarding BrightBay thread. Priyom proposed margin constraints and adjustments to SLA credits. We need: 

- Legal: any language we should never concede on (indemnity, liability caps, data residency)?
- Contract: confirm the SOW/transition milestones we should require before credits vest (e.g., go-live validation window).
- Pricing: is the 30% / 20% tiering workable? Any suggestions for a simpler framing for procurement?

They want a Wednesday deliverable. Quick notes inline would be great.

— Diego
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightBay — legal/commercial guardrails

Diego —

Quick legal/commercial bullets: 

- Do not apply credits to any amounts subject to third-party pass-through charges (e.g., cloud egress) — those should be reconciled separately.
- Credits vest in two tranches: 50% at onboarding acceptance (post-go-live verification) and 50% after 90 days of sustained usage above the agreed baseline. This prevents early churn abuse.
- Add a 120-day cap on credit claims after termination/transition.
- For SLOs: use objective telemetry tags (route id + timestamp) to adjudicate misses; avoid subjective language.

I’ll mark up the SOW with minimal required milestones and a sample acceptance checklist.

— Hannah
Senior Contracts Counsel

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 13:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightBay — commercial redlines and SOW notes

Diego / team —

Two quick redlines from the contract side: 

1) Limit the effective credit cap to the lesser of (a) agreed trade-in cap and (b) 6 months of projected Redwood ARR contribution — keeps exposure bounded.
2) Define an onboarding escape clause: if BrightBay’s integration requires >4 weeks of professional services beyond what’s scoped, we automatically reduce credit tranche 2 by 25% until the extra work is covered.

I’ll attach a one-page redline summary to send to customer.

— Laura
Head of Commercial Contracts

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@brightbay.ai>, BrightBay Procurement <procurement@brightbay.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Updated: transition economics, credit mechanics, and pilot SOW

Ellen —

Appreciate the patience — attached are three artifacts: a compact trade-in worksheet, a short SOW for a 90-day pilot, and a one-page commercial redline summary. Highlights below: 

- Trade-in credit: tiered at 30% (<=6 months remaining), 20% (6–18 months), 10% (>18 months), with a hard cap equal to the lesser of the computed credit or 6 months of anticipated Redwood spend. Credits vest 50% on go-live acceptance and 50% after 90 days of usage above baseline.
- Margin guardrails: we confirm internal margin floor of 38% — if usage patterns breach that within 12 months, a usage true-up will apply.
- SLA uplift: 99.95% option available; missed SLO credits set at 3% monthly (reduced from initial ask). Objective telemetry will be used for adjudication.
- Onboarding caveat: any >4 weeks of unscoped professional services reduces tranche 2 by 25% until PS are covered.

If that reads clean, can you confirm a pilot kickoff week starting June 1? Doc links below.

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: transition-credit-term-sheet.xlsx, Redwood-Draft-SOW-v1.pdf, BrightBay_TCO_sheet.xlsx
Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567, https://www.docusign.com/brightbay/redwood_transition_v1
From: Ellen Park <ellen@brightbay.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBay Procurement <procurement@brightbay.ai>, Derek Sanders <derek.sanders@cloudforge.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated: transition economics, credit mechanics, and pilot SOW

Diego / team —

This looks good and pragmatic. Procurement will run the numbers against CloudForge obligations and get back with one small ask: can we soften the 4-week extra-PS cliff to a 2-week notice + review before credit reduction? The CPO wants to avoid surprises on implementation sequencing.

We’ll aim to confirm kickoff by Friday. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

— Ellen
Head of Platform Strategy, BrightBay
